output.brief: The evidence points mainly to the merit scholarship cut, not the Admissions Office or the portal. Enrolment fell in the Dean's and Merit tiers (yield roughly 45% to 32%), while the no-merit group and the Presidential tier barely moved. Early-action admits, whose decisions were processed on the old system, saw yield fall as much as regular-decision admits (45% to 38% vs 39% to 32%), so the slow portal-era turnaround does not explain the drop. Admits rose and their GPA was stable, so a weaker pool is not the cause. I am fairly confident about the scholarship link, since it is tier-specific and time-ordered, but I have not tested it directly. The merit-reader staffing cut and the missing-document complaints are still unverified. Next steps: have the Finance Committee model restoring Dean's and Merit award levels before next cycle's letters go out. Set a monthly turnaround target for regular-decision files as a low-cost measure. Do not replace the Director on this evidence. Confirm the missing-document issue before any vendor action.
output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe problem and decision analysis, using X2 and X6 as the two collected items.
